term: necessary simple candidates versus one divine nature
resolution: In this fixed interpretation necessary means world-relative NecessaryAt, not necessary per se; pure act means no potency in the supplied three-respect carrier. The existing first-mover simplicity conclusion follows from concrete component priority plus its inclusion premises, not a complete account of every composition. Essence/esse and suppositum/nature equality compare each candidate’s own represented principle values; they do not identify different candidates’ natures. Q11’s IsGod parameter is instantiated by a candidate predicate only to test the theorem interface, without a theological identification or a claim about Trinitarian persons. Two roots share every represented act but have distinct essence values; an independently defended principle would have to exclude that combination. Tagged intrinsic explanation is not efficient self-causation or sufficient noncausal explanation. The Lean carrier and constructor tags are representational devices, not by themselves real genus–difference composition; no absence of that composition is established by omitting its ontology.
